text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Chancellor of Justice Jorma S. Aalto on Monday received clarification from the central bank governor on the alleged leak of Finland's negotiating position when the markka was pegged to ERM. Second finance minister Arja Alho, whose actions are being investigated, regrets being by-passed in the enquiry.
- Four lesser white-fronted geese -- an endangered bird -- to be fitted with transmitters to track their winter migration. @
- Three men charged for spreading counterfeit dollar notes. Police suspect them of belonging to an international syndicate.
DEMARI
- Monetary policy of Finland's central bank was firmly under the president's tutelage during Mauno Koivisto's two terms of office (1981-1994), a new book says.
- By international standards, Finns are highly committed to the goals of their employers but workers' aspirations are often ignored, study shows. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Social and Health Ministry expected to raise pension insurance contributions in November-December to cover a billion markka gap in pension coverage left by bankrupt Elake-Kansa.
- Finnish Outokumpu one of three bidders for partnership in Chilean Los Pelambres copper mine.

- Salomon Brothers expect newsprint prices to fall 15 percent and SC magazine paper to drop 14 percent next year. Pulp prices likely to be around $575 per tonne in 1997, after plunging 35 percent this year, investment bank says. @
- Brokers play key role in determining share prices, new dissertation says.
AAMULEHTI
- Nordic state railway companies exploring opportunities for joint venture to sell freight services.
- Finnish study shows cow's milk milked at night makes rats sleepy -- pointing to potential insomnia cure.
- Minister of Trade and Industry Antti Kalliomaki says state prepared to order a 300-400 million markka ice-breaker from Finnyards, but the troubled dockyard would need other orders. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Almost 150 doctors at University of Turku Hospital threatening to quit because of disagreement over shift-work.
- Finnish sportsmen's clothing -- including NHL ice-hockey star Teemu Selanne's underwear -- bring money at benefit auction for sick children.
